correctness.rationale: The ten exact golden-ratio spectral labels yield a torus Fourier expression for the cycle displacement law. A nonnegative full-support density with moments 1 at zero and -1/2 at ±(1,-2) cancels all nine nontrivial cyclic modes: zero/positive/negative character counts are (0,0,0) for odd shifts and (2,2,2) for even shifts. Fourier inversion proves the uniform torus barycenter. Irrationality of the golden ratio makes every physical-time tail dense, while full support ensures the barycenter lies in the relative interior of its convex image. A finite-dimensional convex density theorem plus Carathéodory gives at most six real times >T. verify.py exhaustively checks the finite spectral labels and differences; an independent numerical grid check corroborates, but is not the proof.

value.rationale: C10 is the first twice-an-odd-prime cycle beyond C6 and a natural golden-ratio-spectrum benchmark for a published randomized quantum-mixing research program. Instantaneous and conventional averaging are both obstructed on this same graph, making the positive exact shared-time law substantive. A single nonnegative spectral character cancels all repeated-eigenvalue Fourier obstructions simultaneously, and a finite six-point bound holds after an arbitrary cutoff; these constitute motivated new structural and sampling information, not a numerical guess or arbitrary parameter tweak.
